prompts:
Create a richly detailed HD PIXEL ART sprite animation sheet matching the exact character style in the two reference images, which show our actual game homepage roster character Lục Phong. References are identity and MATERIAL/DETAIL QUALITY standards. Dark navy tousled spiky hair, small clear warm face with defined eyes, dark forest-green short cloak with narrow ivory/gold woven border, finely modeled engraved silver oval breastplate, layered dark brown leather cuirass and cross straps, tiny metal buckles, dark fitted trousers with seam/fold definition, articulated brown leather gloves, tall brown boots with straps and distinct sole. Slim elegant anime RPG body, same proportions as references. Exactly one plain silver longsword with a refined small brass crossguard, solid natural hilt grasp.

QUALITY CHANGE: Preserve the delicate fine detail and material shading of the homepage reference. Make this a HIGHER NATIVE PIXEL DENSITY version, around 120 native pixels from hair crown to boot sole (rather than the previous 75). Native hair silhouette about 36 pixels wide and 24 high. It must look like beautiful finely shaded handcrafted fantasy JRPG pixel sprites: very clear hair clusters, defined eyes and chin, crisp plate edges/engraving, readable leather stitching and buckles, tiny fabric folds, clean boot straps. Use small crisp angular pixel clusters, selective single-pixel highlights, coherent material shade ramps and restrained dark outlines. NO flat toy/chibi look, giant smooth shiny armour blobs, big gold collar button, broad chunky limbs, simplistic three-color shading, blurred painted texture, noise or random speckles. Rich DETAIL without visual noise. Follow original outfit and head/body ratios, do not simplify the master.

One 6-column by 4-row sprite sheet, all 24 equal cells, transparent PNG, ordered left-to-right/top-to-bottom. Logical cell 192x192, root center near [96,168], crown about y48, sole y167. Every character at the EXACT SAME physical scale and pixel density; same hair/head width, face size, shoulders, torso, leg thickness and boot length. One uniform camera and lighting for the entire sheet. Head never inflates during attack, and moving figures never turn fuzzy. Hair, face, body and outfit are painted as ONE continuous integrated figure per frame, not detachable parts.

Cells 1–4: FRONT-facing idle breathing cycle, right hand holding sword down at side, consistent with original reference.
Cells 5–12: eight FRONT-facing gentle walking steps, left/right contact, toe-off, passing and contact; feet actually alternate and legs bend subtly; natural sword-carrying arm, hilt closed inside fingers, blade follows the actual wrist.
Cells 13–24: twelve FRONT-facing sword-cut frames: exact idle, second hand joins grip, ready blade at shoulder, raise both hands, coiled overhead anticipation, decisive down-forward diagonal cut with torso involvement, impact, low follow-through, settle, recover, return, exact idle. Body proportions remain unchanged, only real articulation moves. Fingers wrap around the hilt between crossguard and pommel; no detached weapon, extra hands or distorted fingers. Include generous weapon clearance inside each cell. The sword must be separable later via its outline and known hand overlap, so keep its shape and hilt geometry consistent.

Actual crisp pixel game art, not smooth illustration with a pixel filter. Transparent outside all sprites; no background, floor, shadow, glow, motion blur, trails, effects, text, grid or numbers.

EDIT TARGET: first image, our existing 24-cell 6-column by 4-row sprite sheet. REFERENCE FOR FINE ART STYLE: second image, the exact game homepage roster character. Preserve the first image's 24 character positions, same relative head/body dimensions, same feet baselines, same camera scale, same action order, same complete-body silhouettes, same grid layout. Do NOT create a newly composed sheet or fit bigger figures into early rows and smaller figures into later rows.

Refine the existing sprites into richer HIGH-DENSITY HD PIXEL ART, about 120 native pixels crown-to-sole rather than 75. Keep the established slim body proportions, small navy spiky hair and warm face. Add real crisp fine pixel detail to hair clusters, eyes/chin, silver breastplate facets and subtle engraving, brown leather straps and tiny metal buckles, clothing seams, restrained cloth folds, glove construction, boot straps and soles. Match the second reference's elegant delicate material rendering, not simplistic toy/cartoon sprites. Restore the reference collar/fastening; no large bright gold collar button. Same dark forest-green short cape with narrow ivory trim, fitted dark brown armour, dark trousers, brown boots. Fine discrete material shade ramps, clean angled pixel clusters and selective one-pixel highlights; NO blurry gradients, fuzzy painted microtexture, random speckles, flat shiny armour blobs or thick muddy outlines. Every idle, walk and attack figure gets the SAME exact detail density and palette. The character must NOT inflate, widen, change skull size or lose detail while moving.

SPECIFIC POSE FIX: the overhead anticipation poses at cells 16 and 17 (row 3, columns 4 and 5) must show BOTH hands clasped together directly above the head and the sword pointing STRAIGHT VERTICALLY UP, aligned with the two hands and forearms. Not tilted to screen-right, not sideways behind the head, not a bent wrist. Crossguard above the top fist, grip firmly enclosed by both hands, pommel behind/below the lower hand, blade rises straight up. Keep the head and torso original size and location, elbows connect anatomically to shoulders. Generous empty clearance above blade, no cell clipping. These are anticipation frames before the same decisive down-forward diagonal cut. The sword is rigid, straight plain steel with small refined brass crossguard. In other poses preserve existing action and sword direction.

The entire hair, face, head, neck, clothes and body remain ONE continuous figure per frame. Sword is drawn clearly with hard silhouette and fingers overlapping hilt so it can be separated for replacement later. No extra fingers/hands/weapons. Transparent background with hard alpha; no ground shadow, light haze, effects, trails, labels, grid lines or text. Do not change the sheet layout, cell centers or body scale while adding detail.
feedback: Chủ dự án nhận xét nét vẽ chưa đẹp; phải ghi rõ quy chuẩn style trước khi vẽ tiếp. Khung giơ tay phải dựng trục kiếm thẳng.
